facts.value: Full 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy and Prudential Indicators, presented as a 9-page Cabinet covering paper (30865) with a 44-page Treasury Management Strategy Statement appendix (30866). Both PDFs held on disk. The covering paper prints high-level summary tables; the tables and prudential indicators that carry the loan book, CFR, liability benchmark, maturity structure, affordability ratios, MRP policy, investment strategy and the MUFG rate forecast sit in the 30866 appendix

source.title: Appendix 1 - Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 (Cabinet 4 February 2026; Council 12 February 2026)

facts.note: Companion paper: 'Appendix A - Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27' (30866), 44 pages, held on disk. Cited as 30866 with page references throughout. Melton Borough Council is a small stock-holding non-metropolitan district in Leicestershire (1,786 HRA dwellings at 31/3/25). The report is signed by Natasha Bailey (Senior Management Accountant) as author, Dawn Garton (Director for Corporate Services) as Chief Officer Responsible, and Cllr Sarah Cox as Portfolio Holder. The paper does not print the letters 'S151' against Dawn Garton but §9.2 refers to 'The Director for Corporate Services reports that the Council complied with this prudential indicator' — the standard S151 form of words. Report header footer on every page reads 'Treasury Management Mid-Year Report 2023-24' (a template footer not updated) while the actual title is 'Treasury Management Strategy and Prudential Indicators 2026-27'; not raised.

facts.value: PWLB £29,315k at 31/12/25 (100% of external borrowing); £31,315k at 31/3/25. Treasury investments £26,940k at 31/12/25 (banks £18,000k 67%, MMFs £6,940k 26%, CCLA property fund £2,000k 7%); £18,160k at 31/3/25. Net treasury investments/(borrowing) -£2,375k at 31/12/25; -£13,155k at 31/3/25. The £2m fall in PWLB in-year is the 'Expected change in Debt' of -£2,000k for 25/26
facts.note: The paper does not print a weighted average interest rate on the loan book, a loan-by-loan schedule, or an actual maturity-structure position (§5.1.3 p.30 prints only the upper/lower LIMITS — 0% and 50% in every band). The £29,315k PWLB is reported as unchanged across the strategy horizon (25/26-27/28), with £1,500k of net new borrowing only in 28/29.

facts.value: £32,602k (25/26 E), £32,389k (26/27 E), £32,180k (27/28 E), £33,523k (28/29 E). General Expenses CFR £1,118k → £905k → £696k → £2,039k; Housing (HRA) CFR flat at £31,484k throughout — 97% of total CFR

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 §2.2 CFR table, p.8 (repeated in §3.1 external debt table, p.14)

facts.note: Total CFR is dominated by the HRA — Housing CFR of £31,484k against total CFR of £32,389k in 26/27 = 97.2% HRA. The Housing CFR is flat because the HRA operates 'no provision for the repayment of debt for either existing or new debt' per the 2022/23 HRA business plan (covering paper §5.2). All CFR movement is on the General Fund side; the small 28/29 uptick (£2,039k) is the only planned GF unsupported borrowing in the plan.

facts.value: PWLB (end) 29,315 → 29,315 → 29,315 → 30,815 (25/26 through 28/29 estimates, £000). OLTL (end) 1,118 → 905 → 696 → 539. Gross debt (end) 30,433 → 30,220 → 30,011 → 31,354. Under-borrowing steady at £2,169k across all four years
facts.note: Verbatim narrative at §3.4 (p.19): 'We do not envisage any borrowing requirement and can use internal resources for 2026/27 where required.' The £1,500k of new borrowing in 28/29 is the only planned drawdown in the strategy period. OLTL (Other Long-Term Liabilities per §2.2 p.8 = PFI + finance leases) runs down through amortisation.

facts.value: £2,169k across 25/26 to 28/29 (unchanged year on year). Steps up from £169k actual at 24/25 as the £2m in-year PWLB repayment lifts under-borrowing then holds flat

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 §3.1 External Debt / Under-borrowing table, p.14

facts.note: The GF Liability Benchmark chart at §2.3 p.9 shows GF Net Loans Requirement at -£10k to -£11k throughout — the GF is a permanent net investor. The HRA chart at §2.3 p.10 shows Loans CFR at £31.5m with Existing Loan Debt Outstanding at ~£29k and Net Loans Requirement at ~£22m. Narrative at covering paper §5.7: 'the Council's HRA borrowing is below the CFR and will reduce over time... it is expected to remain below the liability benchmark after any refinancing.'

facts.value: Non-HRA: -10.29% (24/25 A), -8.90% (25/26 E), -4.44% (26/27 E), -4.14% (27/28 E), -3.25% (28/29 E) — NEGATIVE in every year (investment income exceeds treasury financing costs). HRA: 26.74%, 27.90%, 27.96%, 28.34%, 27.64%

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 §5.1.2 Ratio of Financing Costs to Net Revenue Stream table, p.29

facts.note: The negative Non-HRA ratio is a relatively unusual pattern across the papers we have read (most GF ratios run 2%-15% positive). Consistent with the almost-entirely-HRA balance of the CFR (97% HRA at 26/27). The HRA ratio is high but stable — expected for a stock-holding district with a self-financed HRA and no MRP charge.

Debt per dwelling of £16-17k is a low figure for a stock-holding district. Interest Cover moves 0.28 → 0.16 → 1.22 — a step change of ~8x between 25/26 and 26/27 estimates against the paper's own 'Ideally over 1.10' threshold. Not explained in the paper text. Not derivable inside this repo whether this reflects a change in the numerator basis (net operating income) or the interest denominator (the £2m PWLB repayment does not on its own account for such a jump). Recorded internally as an observation; NOT raised in the email — do not invite a correction on their own ratio construction. Separately, the 'Ratio of Debt to Revenues (%)' column shows 30-36% which appears to be Revenues/Debt (9,423/31,315 = 30.09%) rather than Debt/Revenues (which would be 332%); the label appears inverted. Also not raised.

facts.value: Authorised Limit £46,000k flat across 25/26-28/29 (Debt £45,090k-£45,460k walking up; OLTL £910k-£540k walking down). Operational Boundary £37,000k flat (Debt £29,315k; OLTL £905-539k; Headroom £6,780k-£7,146k)

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 §3.2 Authorised Limit and Operational Boundary tables, pp.14-15

facts.note: Both indicators sit well above expected debt. Covering paper §5.6 notes the Operational Boundary was 'increased to give headroom for temporary borrowing to deal with cashflow should the need arise' following IFRS16 lease changes and the intended 28/29 borrowing. Authorised Limit is the statutory s.3(1) Local Government Act 2003 ceiling.

facts.value: Asset life method (straight line) since 1 April 2008 for all unsupported borrowing including PFI and finance leases. HRA no MRP charge (Major Repairs Reserve + depreciation provide prudent provision). IFRS 16 leases: MRP equals the principal element of the existing rent/charge writing down the balance sheet liability. Capitalisation Direction: asset life applied. Capital receipts on loans to third parties reduce CFR rather than substitute for MRP. No VRP overpayments to date
facts.note: No change from prior year (§4.2 p.23 confirms creditworthiness criteria unchanged). MRP Guidance (2024) expressly referenced. Standard policy for a district with an HRA — nothing distressed. The 2003 Regulations amendment 'from April 2025 to expressly provide that in determining a prudent provision local authorities cannot exclude any amount of CFR from its calculation' is cited (§2.5 p.11).

facts.value: £2m nominal in CCLA property fund since 2017. Valuation £1.841m at 31/12/25 — notional loss £159k (from £158k at 30/9/25). Property Fund Reserve expected £190k at end 25/26 — covers the notional loss. Investment income £712k net of fees since inception (to end September 2025). IFRS 9 statutory override extended to 31/3/29; from 1/4/29 gains and losses must be credited/charged to the General Fund
facts.note: The £1.841m at 31/12/25 against £2m at cost = 92.05% of nominal; the £190k reserve balance approximately equals the £159k notional loss. External Fund Managers section (30866 §4.6 p.27) confirms £7.75m in Money Market Funds at 31/12/25 alongside the £2m CCLA. The 31/3/29 override cliff is a live consideration for any council carrying a pooled fund position — Melton has managed this by building a dedicated reserve.

facts.value: Security first, liquidity second, yield third. Non-specified treasury management investment limit £10m. Country limit minimum sovereign AA- (Fitch), UK exempt; no more than 50% outside UK. Upper limit principal sums invested for longer than 365 days: £10m in each of 25/26, 26/27, 27/28; current £0m in each year. Benchmark overnight 7-day SONIA
facts.note: MUFG Corporate Markets provides the creditworthiness service (§4.2 p.23). Melton uses counterparties from blue/orange (up to 1 year) down to green (up to 100 days) for fixed-term investments up to 1 year in duration (§4.2 p.24). Suggested budgeted investment earnings rate 3.40% for 26/27 (§4.3 p.26).

facts.value: Standard list at §3.8 (PWLB, Local Authorities, Banks, Pension Funds, Insurance Companies, Market long-term/temporary/LOBOs, Stock Issues, Municipal Bonds Agency, Overdraft, Negotiable Bonds, Internal, Commercial Paper, Medium Term Notes, Leases) plus 'UK National Wealth Fund' — a newer addition to the approved list

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 §3.8 Approved Sources of Long and Short-term Borrowing, pp.19-20

facts.note: Melton has no LOBOs (the loan book is 100% PWLB per §3.1 p.13). The UK National Wealth Fund inclusion is worth noting but only if we have seen enough other approved-source lists to say it is unusual, which is a claim to make cautiously. Not raised in the email.

facts.value: MUFG Corporate Markets forecast dated 22 December 2025. Bank Rate 3.75% (Mar-26) falling to 3.25% (Dec-26 through Mar-29). 5-year PWLB 4.60% (Mar-26) falling to 4.10% by Mar-27. Current PWLB (certainty) rates at 22.12.25 p.m.: 5y 4.81%, 10y 5.39%, 25y 6.01%, 50y 5.78%. Target end-Q4 2027: 5y 4.10%, 10y 4.70%, 25y 5.30%, 50y 5.10%

source.title: TMSS 2026/27 §3.3 Prospects for Interest Rates and Appendix 5.2 Interest Rate Forecasts, pp.16-18 and 31

facts.note: Verbatim borrowing advice (p.18): 'better value can be obtained at the shorter end of the curve (<5 years PWLB maturity/<10 years PWLB EIP) and short-dated fixed LA to LA monies should also be considered.' MUFG's long-run Bank Rate neutral remains 3.5%. Report expects a rate cut Q2 2026 to 3.5% then Q4 2026 to 3.25%. Forecast reached Cabinet 4 February 2026 and Council 12 February 2026 — a 6-7 week gap between forecast date and Council decision, on the shorter end of what we see.

facts.value: Under-borrowed position maintained. 'We do not envisage any borrowing requirement and can use internal resources for 2026/27 where required' (§3.4 p.19). Rescheduling considered whilst premature redemption rates remain elevated 'only if there is surplus cash available to facilitate any repayment' (§3.6 p.19). Council would only borrow to fund capital investment with a clearly defined business case; PWLB preferred
facts.note: Contingent responses: postpone borrowing if sharp rise risk; draw fixed rate now if sharper fall risk (§3.4 p.18-19). The strategy is coherent with the position — the book is HRA-attributable long-dated PWLB at ~3.5% weighted, and there is no near-term refinancing spike to work with. The £2m repayment already made in 25/26 fits the surplus-cash constraint at §3.6.

summary.text:
Melton Borough Council's Treasury Management Strategy and Prudential Indicators 2026/27 — a 9-page Cabinet covering paper (30865) with a 44-page appendix Treasury Management Strategy Statement (30866). Both PDFs on disk. Melton is a small stock-holding district in Leicestershire with 1,786 HRA dwellings and a book that is essentially all HRA. Report to Cabinet 4 February 2026, then Council 12 February 2026.

Loan-book reconciliation TIES to the pound. Our PWLB file holds 10 loans totalling £29,315,344 at a weighted 3.6352% against the paper's §3.1 (30866 p.13) £29,315k PWLB position at 31/12/25 (100% of external borrowing). The paper does not print a weighted rate or a loan count. The 25/26 in-year fall of £2m from £31,315k at 31/3/25 to £29,315k at 31/12/25 matches the 'Expected change in Debt' -£2,000k on the External Debt table (p.14).

Balance-sheet identity ties across all four forecast years. CFR walks 32,602 → 32,389 → 32,180 → 33,523 (§2.2 p.8); actual gross debt at 31 March walks 30,433 → 30,220 → 30,011 → 31,354 (§3.1 p.14); under-borrowing holds at £2,169k across 25/26 to 28/29. CFR − PWLB − OLTL = under-borrowing to £1k rounding in every year. Identity clean.

The book is 97% HRA. Total CFR £32,389k at 26/27 comprises Housing CFR £31,484k (flat throughout because the 2022/23 HRA business plan provides for no repayment provision) and General Expenses CFR £905k. The Non-HRA ratio of financing costs to net revenue is negative in every year (-10.29% → -3.25%), meaning the General Fund's investment income exceeds its treasury financing costs. It is a relatively unusual pattern in the papers we have read.

Rate outlook is MUFG dated 22 December 2025. Central call is Bank Rate falling to 3.25% by Dec-26 and held through Mar-29; 5-year PWLB certainty from 4.81% (22/12/25 p.m.) to 4.10% by end Q4 2027. Council decision was 12 February 2026 — a 6-7 week gap between forecast date and Council, on the shorter end of what we see.

The pooled fund line has a 2029 cliff. £2m in the CCLA property fund since 2017, valued £1.841m at 31/12/25 (notional loss £159k). Dedicated Property Fund Reserve expected £190k at end 25/26 — covers the notional loss. IFRS 9 statutory override extended to 31/3/29; from 1/4/29 gains and losses must be credited/charged to the General Fund. Standing consideration for any council carrying a pooled position.

Two items INTERNAL ONLY. (i) 'Ratio of Debt to Revenues (%)' at §5.1.2 p.30 shows 30-36% which appears to be Revenues/Debt (9,423/31,315 = 30.09%) not Debt/Revenues (which would be 332%) — likely a label inversion. Not raised. (ii) 'Interest Cover (Ideally over 1.10)' moves 0.28 → 0.16 → 1.22 → 1.13 → 1.26 — two years below the paper's own threshold then a step change; construction not stated. Not raised — do not invite a correction on their own ratio.

Contacts. Dawn Garton, Director for Corporate Services, is the Chief Officer Responsible on the front sheet and the §9.2 third-person reference suggests she is the S151, but the paper does not print those letters. Address her by her printed title. Natasha Bailey (Senior Management Accountant) is the report author. Both emails are on the paper front sheet. Cllr Sarah Cox is the Lead Member — a councillor, not to be emailed.

Email drafted around the loan-book match, the HRA-dominant book with the GF as a net investor, the 2029 IFRS 9 cliff against the property fund, and the standing note on the liability benchmark. No advice. Every figure quoted is sourced to a page.

officer.body:
Dear Dawn,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on the Treasury Management Strategy that went to Council on 12 February. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The strategy reads cleanly and the appendix does the work most councils leave for a Cabinet member to guess at, so this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

A short check first, because it's the thing that settles the question of whether the reading was real. Our PWLB file holds 10 loans totalling £29,315,344 against Melton at a weighted 3.6352%, which reconciles to the pound against the £29,315k you print at paragraph 3.1 of the strategy statement at 31 December 2025. The £2m fall in-year from the March position reconciles too — that's the 'Expected change in Debt' line on the same table. Your paper doesn't print a weighted rate or a loan count so those two are ours alone, but the principal matches exactly.

The shape underneath it is what stood out. Your Housing CFR of £31,484k sits inside a total CFR of £32,389k — 97% of the underlying borrowing need is HRA. The General Fund side of the ratio of financing costs to net revenue at page 29 is consequently negative in every year, from -8.90% in 2025/26 to -3.25% by 2028/29 — investment income above treasury financing costs on the General Fund. That's a relatively unusual pattern in the papers we've read; most General Fund ratios in the library run 2 to 15 points positive. Almost the entire external debt sits behind the HRA book, and the maturity buckets in our file line up with that — the long-dated cohort at ~3.5% is the HRA-vintage debt, which is exactly where the £29m concentrates.

The other paragraph worth flagging is 5.12 in the covering paper — the CCLA property fund at £2m nominal, £1.841m at 31/12/25, with the notional £159k loss almost exactly covered by the £190k in the Property Fund Reserve. That is well managed. The line to keep an eye on is the IFRS 9 statutory override — extended to 31 March 2029 as the paper notes, but from 1 April 2029 any gain or loss on the fund must be credited or charged to the General Fund. Between now and then is the runway to decide the position; three years and a bit sounds long until it isn't. We don't sell property fund advice and there's no recommendation in this — the override cliff is simply the standing question every council carrying a pooled position has to time.

Where it would be quickest to look on our side is pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis — that's where the sector's loan books are priced daily against the DMO's premature repayment curve. Your own book prices at an indicative settlement below par given how low the weighted rate sits against today's curve; break costs there are indicative only and only the DMO can quote a real number. Your paragraph 3.6 says rescheduling is considered 'only if there is surplus cash available to facilitate any repayment', and the £2m repayment already made in 25/26 fits that constraint — the page just lets you see the position of the wider book at any point, without doing anything with it.

One standing point because CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates will put it in front of every S151: the liability benchmark pathway becomes central to how the whole strategy is framed. Your section 2.3 sets out the four components verbatim from the Code and prints the two LB charts. An interactive version tied to our rate feeds is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — useful because the HRA chart's Existing Loan Debt Outstanding line runs off in the 2050s and 2060s, and seeing how the market's forward curve moves against that pathway is easier live than in a snapshot.

On training, three fit the paper. The liability benchmark pathway is the natural complement to your section 2.3. Investment strategy for HRA-dominant councils is closest to Melton's position — a General Fund that is a net investor with the entire debt book behind the housing service. And IFRS 9 statutory override — the 2029 cliff picks up the property fund question at paragraph 5.12.
